linelore in your editor, and an opt-in summary from your own model. This is the v0.4 milestone from the [roadmap](https://github.com/Blackman99/linelore/blob/v0.4.0/ROADMAP.md).

## Added
- **Editor integrations** in [`editors/`](https://github.com/Blackman99/linelore/tree/v0.4.0/editors). Copy one; nothing to install from a marketplace.
  - **Neovim 0.9+.** `:Linelore` or your keymap, `:'<,'>Linelore` for a range. The float opens at the cursor with focus in it. `⏎`/`gx` opens the link you're on, `o` the PR, `y` copies, `q` closes. The lookup runs in the background, and the float tells you when the buffer has unsaved changes (line numbers come from the file on disk).
  - **Emacs 27.1+.** `M-x linelore`, with the region active for a range. Opens `*linelore*` below, with links as buttons. `TAB` walks the links, `o` opens the PR, `w` copies, `g` looks again. Text wraps under its label at the window width.
  - **VS Code.** Three tasks (this line, a range of lines…, open the pull request), plus `Ctrl+Alt+L` / `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+L` bindings. Output goes to a terminal panel, where URLs are clickable.
  - **Helix 25.07+.** `space l l` for the line or selection, `space l o` for the PR, through `:sh` and Helix's new command expansions.
  - Neovim and Emacs parse `--json`. The fields they read are pinned by tests, and a new CI job runs Neovim, Emacs and Helix headless; a missing editor fails the job rather than being skipped. [Editors docs](https://blackman99.github.io/linelore/docs/editors/).
- **`--summarize`, opt-in and labelled.** It hands the facts to a model command *you* configured, via `--summarize-cmd 'llm -m gpt-4o-mini'` or `LINELORE_SUMMARIZE_CMD`. Anything that reads a prompt on stdin works: `llm`, `ollama run`, your company's CLI. The answer is printed after the facts under `Summary (generated by <program>, may be wrong; not checked by linelore)`.
  - linelore bundles no model, key or network call. Setting the variable alone never runs anything.
  - In `--json` the answer is a separate `model_summary` field (`by`, `text`, `error`, `disclaimer`), and every fact field is the same as without it.
  - If the command is missing, fails, prints nothing or times out (`LINELORE_SUMMARIZE_TIMEOUT`, 120 s by default; the whole process group is stopped), you get a one-line reason on stderr and exit code 4. The facts are still printed.
  - Output is cleaned of terminal escapes and capped at 4,000 characters. `ollama run`'s word-wrap redraws are replayed, not left as doubled letters.
  - Neovim and Emacs show the summary in its own labelled section (`summarize = true`, `linelore-summarize`, or `C-u M-x linelore` for one time).
  - Tried end to end with a local Qwen2.5 1.5B through ollama. Its summary of the example above credits the single `value_changed` check to the wrong reviewer, which is why the label says "may be wrong". [Summaries docs](https://blackman99.github.io/linelore/docs/summaries/).

## Site
- The landing page has a new section, "In your editor". It shows each plugin's real output for the line above, with a one-time tour through the four editors.

## Install
```bash
pipx install git+https://github.com/Blackman99/linelore@v0.4.0
# or
pip install https://github.com/Blackman99/linelore/releases/download/v0.4.0/linelore-0.4.0-py3-none-any.whl
```

Python 3.9+, no dependencies. Full changelog: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/Blackman99/linelore/blob/v0.4.0/CHANGELOG.md)
